t: You're looking at numbers twenty-five to thirty-six Belgrave Square, a nineteenth-century terrace in Belgravia. It was designed by George Basevi, who also designed Belgrave Square as a whole. Basevi worked in both Neoclassical and Gothic Revival styles and was a pupil of Sir John Soane. Beyond London, he designed the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge. He was also surveyor to the Guardian Assurance Company, to the trustees of Smith's Charity, and to the Thurloe estate.
